properties.name: /why: the reasons behind an existing system are recorded from its designer, and a recalled reason says so
properties.rationale: Built on Anthony's word, 2026-09-23 ("let's implement the /why skill that we brainstormed"), with the scope he chose: the skill plus the honest record it needs — a recalled marker, old fixes kept out of rules written for new work, and a script that groups the history. The payoff (showing an agent a feature's reasons before it edits a file) is deliberately NOT built and the skill says so. Parking was reused for the forward-only exemption rather than a new 'historical' field, because the design already uses it for exactly this (228 pre-rule fixes) and it needs the owner's accepted ruling. Measured while building: git log with line counts took 67 s on this repository's 1,067 commits (the design export is diffed at every commit) against 0.14 s for file names only, so the script counts lines only for typo candidates.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: New served skill `why` (/why) and kit script tools/why_history.py; ChangeEvent gains `rationale_basis` and `commits` (schema/temporal.yaml), written by add_change_event along with `repair`/`stands_in_for`; the confirmation ledger counts recalled changes apart and never as an examination; repair_report counts unstated recalled repairs apart; adopt's Phase 3 points to the skill.
